newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. official sees '97 film, TV production gains.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. official sees '97 film, TV production gains.

text.p: The head of the New York City office that coordinates local film and television production said Monday that total expenditures by producers this year could top the record results in 1996.
"If it is not equal to or past 1996 (results), it will be very, very close," Patricia Reed Scott, commissioner of the Mayor's Office of Film, Theater and Broadcasting, told Reuters in an interview.
"It looks like a very heavy fall schedule," she said.
Direct expenditures by movie and TV companies totalled $2.23 billion in 1996, and $2.0 billion in 1995.
Another key measure is the total number of shooting days. In 1996, the total was 21,286; 20,187 in 1995; and 18,003 in 1994, according to Scott, who added that 1995 and 1996 were record-breakers.
Scott said one indication the 1997 schedule was robust was that nine major feature films --an unusually high total -- were shot entirely in New York during the winter months.
Aside from movies and television series and films, the office tallies commercials, music videos and documentaries.

While 1996, was a "barnburner, and loaded toward the front half of the year, this year is not loaded toward the front half...This year in the second half, more major movies are shooting here," Scott said.
In 1996, 201 films were made in New York, along with about 100 TV series. Scott did not have year-to-date figures for 1997.

Part of the reason for the increased business, Scott said, was an agreement reached between the International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE) Local 52 and movie and TV producers in 1991.
Among other changes, the union, which supplies movie craft crews, agreed to provide less expensive crews to lower-budget films.
IATSE officials were not available for comment.

Among films now shooting in New York are: "Meet Joe Black," a Universal production starring Anthony Hopkins and Brad Pitt; and "The Object of My Affection," a 20th Century Fox production starring Alan Alda and Jennifer Aniston.
Universal is a unit of Seagram Co Ltd, and 20th Century is a unit of News Corp.
